title: 1996 AHSME Problem 1
statement: The addition below is incorrect. What is the largest digit that can be changed to make the addition correct? \[ \begin{array}{r} 641\\ 852\\ {}+973\\ \hline 2456 \end{array} \]

solutions.text: The three addends total \(641+852+973=2466,\) which is \(10\) too large. Changing the tens digit \(7\) in \(973\) to \(6\) lowers the sum by \(10\) and gives \(2456.\) No larger listed digit can make that change, so the correct answer is D.
hints: Compare the displayed sum with the actual sum of the three addends
The correction must lower the total by one unit in a particular place
